programming_tips.topic: G05.1 AI Contour Control (AICC) on Fanuc 0i-MF Plus
programming_tips.code_example:
G05.1 Q1 (enable AICC — nano smoothing + predictive feed)
(3D finishing moves here)
G05.1 Q0 (cancel AICC before tool change)
programming_tips.description: G05.1 Q1 activates AI Contour Control (AICC) with nano smoothing on the 0i-MF Plus. This engages the 100-block lookahead buffer with predictive feed rate adjustment for smooth 3D contouring. Use for all 3D finish machining. The controller dynamically adjusts feed rate at corners and tight curves to maintain programmed tolerance. Always cancel with G05.1 Q0 before M06 tool change.
gotchas: AICC must be canceled before tool change — failure to cancel can cause erratic motion on next tool
AICC mode overrides feed rate at tight corners — actual feed may be lower than programmed F value
Not effective for 2D pocket milling — use standard G01 for 2D
Requires macro option to be installed on 0i-MF Plus

programming_tips.topic: Rigid Tapping G84 with M29 Setup
programming_tips.code_example:
S500 M03
M29 S500 (engage rigid tap mode — MUST match spindle S)
G84 Z-18.0 R2.0 F1.5 (M10x1.5 rigid tap, F=pitch)
G80 (cancel canned cycle)
programming_tips.description: Fanuc 0i-MF Plus requires M29 before G84 for rigid tapping. The S value in M29 MUST match the current spindle speed. F value equals the thread pitch in mm (G21) or inches (G20). The DNM 5700 direct-coupled spindle provides excellent rigid tap performance up to M20. For larger taps, reduce RPM. Double-pass (J2) is available for improved thread quality in tough materials.
gotchas: M29 S value MUST match the active S speed — mismatch causes tap breakage
F value = thread pitch, NOT feed rate — F1.5 means 1.5mm pitch, not 1.5mm/min
Always cancel with G80 after tapping cycle complete
Maximum rigid tap speed depends on hole depth and pitch — consult Doosan tap chart
For left-hand threads, use G84 with M04 spindle direction

programming_tips.topic: G73 High-Speed Peck Drilling vs G83 Deep Hole Peck
programming_tips.code_example:
(G73 — short retract, chip break, fast cycle)
G73 Z-25.0 R2.0 Q5.0 F250 (short retract peck)
(G83 — full retract, chip clear, deep holes)
G83 Z-60.0 R2.0 Q8.0 F150 (full retract peck)
programming_tips.description: G73 retracts a small amount (parameter 5114, default 1mm) to break the chip, then feeds back to the bottom. Much faster than G83 for shallow-medium holes (<5xD). G83 retracts fully to R-plane to evacuate chips — required for deep holes (>5xD) or gummy materials (stainless, titanium) that pack chips. On the DNM 5700, G73 is 30-40% faster than G83 for equivalent hole depths.
gotchas: G73 in gummy materials can pack chips and break drills — use G83 for stainless/titanium
Q value is the peck depth, not the retract amount
G73 retract distance is set by parameter 5114 — verify it is appropriate for your chip formation
For deep holes >10xD, reduce Q peck depth to 1-2x drill diameter

programming_tips.topic: Fanuc Macro B Variables on 0i-MF Plus
programming_tips.code_example:
#100 = 10.0 (local variable — cleared on M98/M99)
#500 = 25.4 (persistent variable — survives power off)
#3006 = 1 (ALARM with message)
IF [#500 GT 50.0] GOTO 100
#101 = #5021 (read current machine X position)
programming_tips.description: Fanuc Macro B on 0i-MF Plus supports custom programming with variables, arithmetic, logic (IF/GOTO/WHILE), and system variable access. Key ranges: #100-#199 (local, cleared per subprogram), #500-#599 (persistent, saved to memory), #5021-#5023 (current machine position XYZ), #5041-#5043 (current work position XYZ), #3006 (generate alarm). Maximum 4-level nesting depth on 0i-MF.
gotchas: 0i-MF Plus supports only 4 nesting levels (vs 10 on 30i/31i) — plan macro structure carefully
Writing to #500-#599 saves to non-volatile memory — avoid high-frequency writes in loops
#3006 = N generates alarm N and stops program — useful for error trapping in macros
Some system variables are read-only — writing to them silently fails, no alarm generated

programming_tips.topic: G10 Programmable Work and Tool Offset Input
programming_tips.code_example:
(Set G54 work offset from probe measurement)
G10 L2 P1 X[#500] Y[#501] Z[#502]
(Set tool 1 length offset)
G10 L10 P1 R5.0 Z100.0
(Incremental offset adjust)
G10 L12 P1 Z0.01 (add 0.01mm to G54 Z)
programming_tips.description: G10 L2 sets work offset values programmatically (L2=absolute, L12=incremental). P1=G54, P2=G55...P6=G59. G10 L10 sets tool geometry offsets. G10 L11 sets tool wear offsets. Extremely useful for automated probe-and-set routines where the probe macro calculates the offset and G10 writes it directly. On the DNM 5700 this enables fully automated part setup.
gotchas: G10 L2 P-number: P0=common shift, P1=G54, P2=G55, etc. — off-by-one errors are common
G10 overwrites existing offset values (L2) or adds to them (L12) — know which you need
Always verify G10-written offsets before cutting — a macro bug writing wrong values causes crashes
G10 L10/L11 tool offsets: P is tool number, not pocket number

programming_tips.topic: G68 Coordinate Rotation for Bolt Patterns
programming_tips.code_example:
(Drill 6 holes on 100mm PCD at 60-deg spacing)
G90 G54 G00 X50.0 Y0
(Hole 1 at 0 degrees)
G83 Z-20.0 R2.0 Q5.0 F200
G80
G68 X0 Y0 R60.0 (rotate 60 degrees)
(Hole 2)
G83 Z-20.0 R2.0 Q5.0 F200
G80
(repeat with R120, R180, R240, R300)
G69 (cancel rotation)
programming_tips.description: G68 rotates the active coordinate system around a specified X/Y center point by angle R. Essential for bolt circles, pattern rotation, and fixture compensation when a part is clamped at an angle. Cancel with G69. On the DNM 5700, G68 works with all canned cycles and cutter compensation.
gotchas: G68 rotation center (X/Y) is in the current work coordinate system, not machine coordinates
G69 cancel MUST be issued before tool change — rotated coordinates affect G28 home motion
Nested G68 calls are NOT supported on 0i-MF — cancel first rotation before starting second
G68 with G41/G42 cutter comp: compensation is applied AFTER rotation — verify direction is correct

programming_tips.code_example:
O0001 (PROGRAM NAME)
G00 G17 G40 G49 G54 G80 G90
G28 G91 Z0 (home Z first — clears tool)
G28 G91 X0 Y0 (home XY)
T01 M06 (first tool change)
G43 H01 Z100.0 (activate TLO at safe Z)
programming_tips.description: Every program on the DNM 5700 should start with the standard Fanuc safety line that resets all modal codes to a known state. G17=XY plane, G40=cancel cutter comp, G49=cancel TLO, G54=select WCS1, G80=cancel canned cycles, G90=absolute mode. Always home Z first to clear the workpiece before any XY motion.
gotchas: Omitting G49 is the #1 cause of Z-axis crashes — ALWAYS include it in the safe start
G80 prevents lingering canned cycle from previous program
Home Z before XY to avoid dragging tool across workpiece
Add G69 if any programs use G68 rotation — rotation persists across M30 on some firmware

programming_tips.topic: Doosan Coolant System — Flood and Optional TSC
programming_tips.code_example:
M08 (flood coolant on — standard)
M51 (through-spindle coolant on — optional TSC)
G83 Z-50.0 R2.0 Q8.0 F150 (deep drill with coolant)
G80
M59 (TSC off)
M09 (flood off)
programming_tips.description: The DNM 5700 has a 400L coolant tank with flood coolant as standard. Optional through-spindle coolant (TSC) is available. The large table (1300x570mm) benefits from multiple coolant nozzles positioned for both left and right side operations. Use flood (M08) for general milling, TSC (M51) for deep drilling and tapping.
gotchas: TSC requires through-coolant tool holders — standard ER collet chucks block the path
M51/M59 are Doosan-specific TSC codes — verify against your machine's M-code list
400L tank provides extended run time but check concentration daily — evaporation concentrates coolant
Position coolant nozzles toward the cut before starting — the 1050mm X travel means nozzles may not reach far ends of table

source.handbook_title: Doosan DNM 5700 Vertical Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.topic: Large Table Strategy — Using 1050mm X Travel Effectively
programming_tips.description: The DNM 5700 has a 1300x570mm table with 1050mm X travel — significantly larger than most BT40 VMCs. Strategies for maximizing this: (1) Use dual-vise setups with G54/G55 for two parts side by side, (2) Use G54.1 extended offsets for multi-part tombstone or fixture plate layouts, (3) Consider that spindle thermal growth affects the far ends of the table more — probe reference part at each end for critical tolerance work, (4) ATC arm is on the left — avoid placing parts that require many tool changes on the far right side to minimize non-cutting time.
gotchas: Thermal growth in X direction can reach 15um over the full 1050mm travel — significant for tight-tolerance work
Heavy fixtures at table extremes reduce Y-axis rapid rate due to table mass
The 570mm Y travel limits large-diameter circular features — verify part fits within Y envelope
Coolant nozzles may need repositioning when working at different X positions

source.handbook_title: Doosan DNM 5700 Vertical Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.code_example:
G54.1 P1 (select extended offset 1)
(machine part 7)
G54.1 P2 (select extended offset 2)
(machine part 8)
G54 (back to standard G54)
programming_tips.description: G54.1 Pxx provides 48 additional work offsets on the 0i-MF Plus, beyond the standard G54-G59. This is 54 total work offsets, ideal for multi-part fixture plates on the large DNM 5700 table. Set offset values on the Work Offset extension page. Combine with G10 L2 and probing for automated multi-part setup.
gotchas: G54.1 P1-P48 are separate from G54-G59 — they are NOT aliases
Not all CAM post processors support G54.1 — some use G154 Pxx instead (Haas convention)
Verify your specific 0i-MF Plus firmware supports all 48 — some older firmware supports only 24
